tech_evidence.names: Washable Stretch Crepe ('From France, our iconic textural knit … packs beautifully'), Washable Flex Ponte; licensed TENCEL Lyocell
tech_evidence.owned: house names (fabric bought in); TENCEL licensed

craft_evidence.owned: for second life only — EILEEN FISHER Renew takes back and resells or remakes worn garments (eileenfisherrenew.com); no owned first-life factory stated
craft_evidence.makers: yes, off the product page — the journal names Fair Trade Certified cut-and-sew factories (PT Tainan, North Jakarta; PT Ungaran, Semarang) and what they make; product pages name none
craft_evidence.mills: no — fabric origin is placed but not named ('Spun in Italy', 'From France')
craft_evidence.madein: 80 of 80 state a country: Vietnam 26, Indonesia 20, Peru 13, USA (of imported materials) 8, China 6, Romania 5, Cambodia
craft_evidence.heritage: dated: 'Reflecting the Future Since 1984' (journal); not placed on the pages read
craft_evidence.process: partly — garment dyeing, Fair Trade factory visits and the Renew take-back are described; first-life making is not
craft_evidence.reasoning: Every sampled page states the country, and the brand names two of its Fair Trade cut-and-sew factories and what they make; it owns none of its first-life making. Renew is owned second-life remaking, not production of the range.
